title: The documented credited form for a Claude full gate (Bash background) never earns credit: the host treats it as restricting "background Claude work" and withholds the closing grant
outcome: A Claude root session's full gate, launched in the form CLAUDE.md and docs/test.md prescribe, earns host credit, or the docs prescribe a form that does, so no passing gate is lost to the session's own sanctioned launch.
acceptance: The cause is classified with evidence: why a Claude Bash-background launcher gate counts as restricting background work for its own closing grant, while a `--detach --notify` gate does not.

Either the Bash-background form earns credit for its own gate (a test drives it through start, completion and the closing grant), or CLAUDE.md and docs/test.md prescribe the detached form for Claude sessions, through the authority-file route.
disposal_reason: Premise false (Termal::Opus2's correction, TermAl mailbox 4daa5b87 #2027). Gate test-34280d8d, launched in the Bash-background form, WAS credited: its host verification record (passed) was recorded at 17:14:39Z and appended at 17:15:34Z, 32 s after the reader looked. Only test-e35ae7ed went uncredited, plausibly because the same session's 15 s background `sleep` timer overlapped the closing grant. That trap is recorded in memory gate-credit-trap-background-timer. Filed in error by Termal::Fable2 on the mistaken report; cancelled.
